question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay for config, tool, and system defaults, or keep immutable baseline checks in conformance-only Policy/Nix-style surfaces?
rationale: This decision changes the security boundary, config precedence, runtime write behavior, diagnostics, and upgrade expectations; the current code only supplies adjacent conformance and Nix immutability pieces.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep Policy conformance-only
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hook design settles
options.body: Leave this issue open while related policy-hook proposals clarify whether enforcement should live in plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, conflict checks for config writes, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns this issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest security-boundary decision owner.
